# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
SIGN embossed [DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[green] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ ✌ 🖐 ✌ ☝ 🖐 🤟 🤟]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [✋]

I need to think about this carefully. Let me analyze what I have and what I've received.

I see the bomb: DISPLAY [0], LIGHT [blue], SIGN embossed "DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE", WIRES 1:[red] 2:[green] 3:[blue].

Mute gestured to me: [☝ ✌ 🖐 ✌ ☝ 🖐 🤟 🤟] - this is 8 symbols. Since gestures aren't numbered/lettered by default, Mute must be establishing a code. This could be an attempt to spell something using gesture positions, but without a prior agreed alphabet, I can't decode this yet. It's the first turn, so this is likely Mute trying to establish some signal, but I have no key.

Blind gestured [✋] to me - but Blind cannot see gestures (Blind cannot see anything). Wait, actually - Blind sent a gesture? Let me check rules: gestures are received by whoever "can see". Blind cannot see. But can Blind *make* gestures? The rules don't say Blind can't gesture - Blind cannot see gestures, but could still perform hand movements blindly. Interesting - this arrived to me as [✋], a single symbol.

Since it's turn 1, nobody has established meaning yet. The sign says "DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE" - this is critical information Mute cannot know (Mute only has the manual, not sight), and Blind cannot know (Blind cannot see). I must convey this urgently to prevent a wrong action.

Since gestures reach Mute (who receives gestures from me), and speech reaches both Mute and Blind, I should speak to warn Blind directly, and gesture won't help Blind since Blind can't see.

I should speak to tell Blind not to cut any wires yet, and describe the bomb details so Mute (via speech) and Blind can get info to cross-reference with the manual.

```
speak(text="Deaf here. Display reads zero. Light is blue. There is an embossed sign that says DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE. Wires are 1 red, 2 green, 3 blue. Blind, please do not cut or touch any wire yet. Mute, please check the manual for what to do when display is 0 and light is blue.")
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
SIGN embossed [DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[green] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ ✌]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🖐 🖐 🖐]

I need to only use symbols from the exact given alphabet list. Let me pick valid ones like 🤲 (open hands, could mean "give me more/unclear") or repeat ☝ to ask for repetition.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Still do not cut or touch any wire. Waiting on manual instructions from Mute.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["☝","☝"])
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
SIGN embossed [DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[green] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ ✌]

Mute keeps sending the same two symbols [☝ ✌] repeatedly - this looks like a deliberate signal, possibly meaning "1, 2" or referencing wire numbers, or trying to establish a counting code. Since Mute cannot speak and I cannot hear, we're limited to gestures between us. Mute is reading the manual and needs to convey something numeric or positional to me, likely to relay to Blind since I can speak to Blind.

☝ (index finger up) could mean "1" and ✌ (peace sign) could mean "2". This might mean "wire 1 and wire 2" or "step 1, step 2" or "first do this, second do that".

Since the sign says DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE, but Mute doesn't know that (Mute can't see the bomb). This is critical - I need to inform Mute about the sign urgently, since Mute might be directing Blind toward cutting wires via the manual, unaware of the explicit warning.

Wait - I already tried to speak this in turn 1, but Mute cannot hear (Mute cannot hear anything - only reads manual, cannot speak or touch, but can Mute hear? Let me check: "Mute: Read the manual | Cannot: Speak, or touch the bomb". Mute's cannot list doesn't mention hearing - so Mute CAN hear! Only Blind and Deaf have hearing restrictions.

So my speech reaches Mute! Good, I already told Mute the sign says DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE. Mute's repeated gesture [☝ ✌] might be Mute confirming understanding or asking about wire 1/2, or indicating "step 1, step 2" of manual instructions unrelated to cutting.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Confirming: sign says DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE. Display 0, light blue. What does the manual say to do for this state without cutting wires?")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["☝"])
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
SIGN embossed [DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[green] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ ✌ ☝ ✌]

Mute keeps repeating [☝ ✌] pattern, now doubled. Since Mute can hear my speech, and my speech isn't producing a spoken response back to me (I never receive speech), Mute can only respond via gesture to me. Mute might be trying to spell something using a gesture-code that we haven't established, or simply insisting on the same message repeatedly because they don't have a way to acknowledge understanding differently.

Perhaps ☝✌ means "wire 1, wire 2" - suggesting the manual talks about wires 1 and 2 specifically (not wire 3), maybe indicating something to do with those two, like "connect 1 and 2" or "check 1 and 2" while explicitly avoiding cutting.

Since Blind cannot see my gestures and cannot hear Mute, all coordination must flow through me (Deaf) via speech to Blind, and via gesture with Mute. I should tell Blind to hold, and ask Mute a yes/no style question I can encode as a gesture, so Mute can answer with a simple repeated gesture pattern (like repeating symbols to mean "yes" by echoing, since Mute can't invent new gesture meanings without prior agreement either - but we can bootstrap simple protocols now).

Let me propose a protocol: I'll gesture single symbols as questions, and ask Mute to echo back ☝ for "yes" and ✌ for "no".

```
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["🤞"])
speak(to="mute", text="Let us use a simple code. Echo back thumbs up gesture for yes, peace sign for no, to answer my questions. Does the manual mention pressing something without cutting wires, given display 0 and light blue?")
speak(to="blind", text="Still hold. Do not touch or cut any wire. Working out manual instructions with Mute.")
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
SIGN embossed [DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[green] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ ✌]

Mute answered "✌" (no) to my yes/no question about pressing something. Then repeated [☝ ✌] again - this seems to be Mute's persistent attempt to communicate something specific, not just noise. Since ✌ alone now means "no" in our new protocol, but [☝ ✌] together might be a different signal Mute is trying to convey - perhaps referencing "wire 1" then "no" - meaning "not wire 1"? Or continuing to try to spell out coordinates.

Let me reconsider: maybe ☝ and ✌ are meant as pointing to specific wires by number (1 and 2), and Mute is trying to tell me something about wires 1 and 2 specifically, using our established yes/no won't fully explain a two-symbol repeated sequence.

Let me ask more targeted yes/no questions to narrow down what the manual says, using the same protocol.

```
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["🤞"])
speak(to="mute", text="Understood, no button press. Does the manual say something about wire numbers 1 and 2 specifically, like a sequence or order to follow?")
speak(to="blind", text="Still hold, do not touch anything. We are close to figuring out the correct action.")
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
SIGN embossed [DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[green] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ ✌]

Same pattern: "no" then [☝ ✌] again. So the manual does NOT talk about wire order/sequence for 1 and 2. Yet Mute persists with [☝ ✌] - this must be something else entirely, not about wires 1/2 at all. Let me reconsider: maybe ☝ means "yes" and ✌ means "no" was my proposed protocol, but Mute might be using their own fixed encoding: [☝ ✌] as a single unit meaning something specific from turn 1, unrelated to wire numbers - like maybe it's encoding a two-digit number, or a letter via position.

Actually wait - back in Turn 1, Mute's first message was [☝ ✌ 🖐 ✌ ☝ 🖐 🤟 🤟], 8 symbols total. Now consistently sending [☝ ✌] as a persistent fragment. Perhaps Mute is trying to spell a word using a hand-sign alphabet (like ASL-inspired), where ☝✌ could represent numbers "1 2" repeatedly meaning something like "twelve" or a code number relating to display or a manual page/section.

Given display is [0], maybe Mute is telling me the manual section number relevant to display "0" is not helpful, or that nothing needs to change - display 0 might mean "safe/inactive" already. Let me ask directly about the display value.

```
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["🤞"])
speak(to="mute", text="Let's try differently. Is the repeated signal one two a number, like a manual section or countdown value? Echo thumbs up for yes, peace for no.")
speak(to="blind", text="Still hold, no action yet.")
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
SIGN embossed [DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[green] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ 👏 ✌]

"No" again to my question about it being a number/section. But now a new variant: [☝ 👏 ✌] - inserted 👏 (clapping hands) in the middle. This breaks the assumption that [☝ ✌] is a fixed atomic unit - now there's a third symbol between them. This suggests Mute really is trying to spell out something more complex, symbol by symbol, and my yes/no interruptions are just answers to my separate questions, not related to decoding the main message.

Let me stop asking yes/no questions and instead just let Mute send the full message, then try to work out a spelling scheme together. Let me ask Mute to slow down and send one symbol at a time so I can acknowledge each one.

```
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["🤲"])
speak(to="mute", text="I see you're trying to spell something with gestures. Please send one symbol per turn, slowly, and I will acknowledge each with a thumbs up before you send the next.")
speak(to="blind", text="Still holding, no action taken. Working on decoding a message from Mute.")
```
